title: Abbasid Caliphate
summary: The Abbasid Caliphate was established in 750, when a movement based in Khorasan ousted the Umayyad caliphs. Its capital was Baghdad, with Samarra as a second capital from 836 to 892, and its most prominent ruler was Harun al-Rashid (r. 786–809). As local rulers declared independence the realm broke apart, and the Mongol destruction of Baghdad in 1258 ended Abbasid rule; a line of "shadow caliphs" continued under the Mamluk Sultanate until 1517.

uncertainty.note: All opened pages give 750 for the dynasty's establishment and 1258 for the end of Abbasid rule in Iraq; the Smithsonian keyword field gives the period as 750–1258.
